record.context_brief: combinatorial flag orbits in convex polytopes
record.original_question: For which pairs of integers (k, d) does there exist a convex d-polytope with exactly k combinatorial flag orbits?

evidence.quote: Problem 26. For what values of k and d is there a convex d-polytope with k combinatorial flag orbits?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P be a convex d-dimensional polytope. A flag of P is a maximal chain F_{-1} ⊂ F_0 ⊂ F_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ F_{d-1} ⊂ F_d in its face lattice, where F_i is an i-dimensional face (with F_{-1} = ∅ and F_d = P). The combinatorial automorphism group Γ(P) is the group of order-preserving bijections of the face lattice of P to itself; it acts on the set of flags of P. The combinatorial flag orbits of P are the orbits of this action, and P is called a k-orbit polytope if it has exactly k such orbits.

Determine the set of pairs of positive integers (k, d) with d ≥ 2 for which there exists a convex d-polytope having exactly k combinatorial flag orbits.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is partially resolved. Cases k=1 (regular convex polytopes) are classically known in every dimension. The combinatorially two-orbit convex polytopes have been completely classified by Matteo: they are exactly the cuboctahedron, icosidodecahedron, rhombic dodecahedron, and rhombic triacontahedron (all 3-dimensional), so the k=2 case is solved. For general k ≥ 3 and various dimensions d, the existence question remains open and is listed among the open problems on k-orbit polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorially two-orbit convex polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: A combinatorially two-orbit convex polytope is isomorphic to one of the cuboctahedron, icosidodecahedron, rhombic dodecahedron, or rhombic triacontahedron.
status_evidence.claim: The k=2 case of the problem has been solved: there are exactly four combinatorially two-orbit convex polytopes, all 3-dimensional.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on k-orbit polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems on combinatorial, geometric, and algebraic aspects of k-orbit polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: The general existence question for convex d-polytopes with exactly k flag orbits remains open and is collected among current research problems.

status_evidence.title: Convex Polytopes and Tilings with Few Flag Orbits (Matteo)
status_evidence.snippet: Classification results for convex polytopes with few flag orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classifications exist for small k, supporting partial-solution status.
